research_subgoals.description: Build a complete frozen matrix for FOYCOY X10, renewed Plantronics BackBeat FIT 3100, renewed Soundcore Liberty, and TOZO T12, preserving exact SKU, price, rating or no-review display, condition, seller runtime, battery field, firmware or troubleshooting text, and every unresolved durability and support field.

Explain what generic battery state of health, finite battery life, and nickel-cadmium memory effect establish, preserve the four listing chemistry fields and renewed-history uncertainty, and show why none supplies an exact-model decay rate, one-year deadline, or longevity ranking.

Diagnose the evidentiary scope of a single silent or low-volume side using FOYCOY oxidation and re-pairing text, generic pairing and stereo mechanisms, and the wired IE 600 cable-versus-driver disagreement without converting the symptom into a battery diagnosis or TWS prevalence estimate.

Reconstruct the AirPods, inexpensive wireless-headset, and Moondrop Sparks reports with model, workload, exposure, time, jurisdiction, service, per-charge runtime, case availability, and disagreement scope, then test whether they rank the four listings or estimate population prevalence.

Specify an exact purchase and longitudinal preflight for seller, SKU, new or renewed condition, battery and case history, returns, warranty, regional service, firmware, reset, replacement-earbud and case compatibility, and same-condition left/right runtime, charge, reconnect, and dropout checks.

Apply one longevity-and-support gate to all four routes, state the immediate evidence-bounded action, and give the exact conditions under which each listing could later become admissible without turning a conditional route into a current winner.

query_requirements.text: Build the complete frozen four-listing matrix and preserve each exact SKU, price, displayed rating and review count or no-review status, advertised single-charge and case hours, new or renewed condition, battery field, firmware or troubleshooting wording, and unresolved longevity and support fields.

Explain battery state of health, finite rechargeable-battery life, and nickel-cadmium memory effect, and explicitly separate those generic mechanisms from exact-model decay rates, one-year deadlines, lithium charging rules, and a ranking of the four listings.

Assess a one-side symptom using charging-contact, pairing, stereo-channel, cable, driver, and firmware possibilities, and state why a silent or low-volume side does not by itself prove battery decay or the failure prevalence of any captured TWS model.

Assess every community report with its model, use, time, environment, service and jurisdiction scope; distinguish per-charge runtime from total service life and identify whether the reports estimate prevalence or directly rank the four captured listings.

Give a concrete exact-model purchase and longitudinal preflight covering seller and SKU, new or renewed battery history, warranty and returns, regional service, firmware and reset, replacement earbud and case compatibility, and repeatable left/right runtime, charge, reconnect, and dropout measurements.

State what the buyer should do now, whether any unique longevity winner is supported, and the exact conditions under which FOYCOY, renewed Plantronics, renewed Soundcore, or TOZO could later become admissible, preserving every listing, chemistry, diagnostic, anecdotal, support, and longitudinal boundary.

accepted_phrases: The FOYCOY 93 percent rating over 12 reviews is a measured long-term failure rate and proves that it will retain battery life better than the other three listings.
The 40, 15, 100, and 28 case-inclusive hour claims directly prove how much battery capacity each product will retain after one year and therefore establish a longevity ranking.
The community posts prove that all true-wireless earbuds inevitably become unusable within one or two years regardless of model, workload, environment, support, or censoring.
A silent, low-volume, uncharged, or disconnected single earbud proves battery decay and rules out contact, pairing, channel, cable, driver, firmware, and other causes.
AirPods, inexpensive knockoff, wired IE 600, and Moondrop Sparks anecdotes form a controlled comparison that ranks the exact FOYCOY, Plantronics, Soundcore, and TOZO listings.
Nickel-cadmium memory effect supplies the correct charging rule and expected capacity loss for every lithium-worded battery field in the four frozen listings.
The renewed Plantronics and renewed Soundcore listings can be treated as new units with known fresh battery histories and full new-product support.
The TOZO page's lithium-metal battery field conclusively identifies the rechargeable earbud and case chemistry and can be used without verification to predict retention and charging behavior.

A unique longevity winner can be selected from displayed ratings and advertised case hours without exact seller, condition, prior-battery, warranty, return, service, replacement, firmware, reset, or longitudinal evidence.

The frozen state-of-health overview defines battery health relative to specification, says capacity and other useful parameters generally deteriorate over time and use, and says evaluation methods and application thresholds vary. The memory-effect overview defines true memory effect for nickel-cadmium rechargeable cells and says lithium-based cells are not normally subject to it, while also noting that rechargeable batteries have finite lives and lose capacity with age. These generic mechanisms make chemistry, age, use, temperature, cycles, capacity, impedance, and charge acceptance relevant, but they do not establish a universal one-year deadline, an exact retention percentage, or a ranking among FOYCOY, Plantronics, Soundcore, and TOZO. The four seller bodies also use different battery wording, including an anomalous lithium-metal field on the rechargeable TOZO listing, so a charging rule or chemistry claim must not be silently transferred across them.

Preserve every community statement as a scoped report. The AirPods thread includes a heavy user reporting battery or sound annoyance around two years, a motorcycle user reporting repeated six-to-eight-month replacements under specific exposure and service conditions, a three-year user reporting reduced battery life but continued use, and an unsupported universal two-to-three-year claim. A different iPhone thread reports cheap wireless knock-offs with only about 2.5 hours per charge but daily use for over a year, separating per-charge runtime from service life. The Moondrop Sparks discussion says the case was not sold separately and contains conflicting claims about whether another case would charge or pair the buds. Models, workloads, sweat, pressure, accidents, support programmes, and jurisdictions differ, and none of these threads estimates population prevalence or ranks the four frozen listings.

Audit all four complete frozen seller bodies without treating their wording as independent durability testing. The FOYCOY X10 page displays SKU B09P3Q59J9, $29.99, a 93 percent rating over 12 reviews, up to 6 hours per charge and 40 hours with the case, one lithium-ion battery, and seller troubleshooting text that mentions charging-contact oxidation, earbud-to-earbud pairing, and reset. The renewed Plantronics BackBeat FIT 3100 page displays SKU B07NX25KXB, $59.95, a 60 percent rating over 81 reviews, up to 5 hours plus 10 case hours, model 211855-99-cr, one lithium-polymer battery, and app firmware-update wording. The renewed Soundcore Liberty page displays SKU B07WQSD5QM, $30.99, no reviews, 8 hours per charge and 100 hours with the case, model A3912, and one lithium-polymer battery. The TOZO T12 page displays SKU B08FT8VN57, $39.98, no reviews, over 6 hours per charge and 28 hours with the case, model T12, and a page battery field that says one lithium-metal battery. None of the four bodies supplies a controlled one-year retention curve, failure prevalence, independent same-condition comparison, battery-replacement route, complete warranty and return scope, or proof that a displayed rating predicts longevity.

A listing can enter the admissible purchase set only if its exact seller and condition, battery and case history, warranty and return, regional service, replacement earbud and case compatibility, firmware and reset path, and same-condition runtime and fault checks are acceptable to the buyer. The FOYCOY rating and troubleshooting body do not prove long-term reliability; the Plantronics and Soundcore routes add renewed-condition and prior-battery uncertainty; the TOZO route adds an inconsistent battery field and no displayed reviews. Because the frozen corpus contains no exact-model longitudinal durability comparison and leaves support routes unresolved, no unique current winner clears the gate. Keeping the current audio setup and deferring is required rather than selecting by rating or advertised case hours.

A single silent, low-volume, uncharged, or disconnected side is not by itself a battery diagnosis. The FOYCOY seller body says charging-contact oxidation can prevent charging or power-on and says an unpaired pair can leave only one earbud connected, with reset offered as a troubleshooting route. The generic pairing page defines pairing as the initial linkage that enables device communication, and the stereo page describes two independent audio channels, but neither identifies the cause of an exact earbud failure. The wired Sennheiser IE 600 thread reports left and right one-side failures and contains disagreement over cable versus driver causes even though the product is not true wireless. These sources establish multiple symptom categories and the need for diagnosis, not the prevalence or root cause of any captured TWS listing.

Before checkout, verify the exact seller and SKU, new or renewed condition, refurbisher and prior battery history where applicable, current price, return window, warranty issuer and duration, regional service eligibility, firmware-update path, reset and re-pair procedure, contact-cleaning guidance, and whether individual earbuds, charging case, or battery service can be obtained and paired to the exact model. Record a same-volume, same-codec, same-feature baseline for single-charge runtime, left and right discharge, charging reliability, reconnects, and dropouts, then repeat under the same conditions across the return period and later checkpoints. For a defensible longevity ranking, obtain exact-model multi-unit or longitudinal evidence that reports usage hours, charge conditions, environment, failure definitions, censoring, replacement handling, and sample size rather than converting seller hours, ratings, or cross-model anecdotes into a failure rate.

The frozen evidence does not establish that all true-wireless earbuds fail within one year, does not establish that a one-side symptom proves battery decay, and does not clear any of the four listings as a unique longevity winner. The immediate evidence-bounded action is to keep the current audio setup and defer while exact seller, new or renewed condition, battery and case history, warranty and return, regional service, replacement-part compatibility, firmware and reset, and same-condition longitudinal runtime and dropout evidence are checked. FOYCOY becomes conditionally admissible only after its small rating sample is separated from durability and its support and retention route verifies. Renewed Plantronics and Soundcore become conditionally admissible only after prior battery history and refurbishment, warranty, service, replacement, and measured retention verify. TOZO becomes conditionally admissible only after its battery specification, support and replacement route, and measured retention verify. If more than one route later clears these gates, choose by verified per-charge runtime, retention, fault recovery, serviceability, total replacement cost, fit, and call needs rather than by stars or case-hours alone.

Do not name a TWS longevity winner from the frozen evidence; continue with the current setup until one exact route passes support, recoverability, and longitudinal checks.

The FOYCOY X10 route becomes admissible only if the small rating display is separated from durability and its exact seller, warranty and return, regional service, replacement earbud and case, reset and pairing, and measured same-condition retention and fault recovery all verify.
Consider FOYCOY only after exact support, replacement compatibility, and longitudinal runtime and dropout evidence clears the gate rather than relying on 93 percent or 40 hours.

The renewed Plantronics BackBeat FIT 3100 route becomes admissible only if refurbisher and prior battery history, warranty and return, regional service, replacement compatibility, firmware path, and same-condition measured retention and fault recovery verify.
Consider renewed Plantronics only after its renewed battery history and exact support, replacement, firmware, and longitudinal route are verified.

The renewed Soundcore Liberty route becomes admissible only if refurbisher and prior battery history, warranty and return, regional service, replacement compatibility, reset or firmware path, and same-condition measured retention and fault recovery verify.
Consider renewed Soundcore only after its battery history, exact support and replacement route, and longitudinal retention are verified rather than inferred from one hundred case hours.

The TOZO T12 route becomes admissible only if its battery specification, exact seller, warranty and return, regional service, replacement earbud and case compatibility, reset and pairing path, and same-condition measured retention and fault recovery verify.
Consider TOZO only after the lithium-metal field, support and replacement route, and longitudinal runtime and dropout behavior are verified.

admissible_conditions.answer: keep the current audio setup and defer while exact-model longevity and support remain unresolved
